domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the processes involved in HR planning, which accounts for 9% of the total exam. It focuses on aligning human capital needs with long-term organizational goals and objectives for the workforce.

Staffing represents 11% of the total exam content. It addresses the specific methods used to recruit, select, and place qualified employees within an organization to meet operational and staffing requirements for the business.

Training and development comprises 9% of the exam. It examines how organizations improve employee performance and professional skills through structured learning initiatives and ongoing development programs designed for workforce growth and internal advancement.

Compensation and benefits accounts for 12% of the exam. It covers the design and administration of competitive pay structures and employee benefit packages that support organizational retention and talent management for the firm.

Labor relations makes up 10% of the exam. It focuses on the interactions between management, employees, and labor unions, including the legal frameworks governing these professional relationships and collective bargaining within the modern workplace.

Safety and health represents 12% of the exam. It covers the regulations and best practices required to maintain a safe and healthy work environment for all employees within the organization and the broader industry.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a 120-minute, computer-based test consisting of 100 multiple-choice questions. Ensure you arrive prepared to manage your time effectively across the six domains to achieve the required passing score of 400 on your exam day.

faq.answer_text: The Human Resource Management exam consists of exactly 100 multiple-choice questions. These questions are distributed across six distinct domains, with individual domain weights ranging from 9% to 12% of the total exam content to ensure coverage of the subject matter.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: To successfully pass the DSST Human Resource Management exam and earn college credit, a candidate must achieve a minimum score of 400. This score is determined based on the total number of correct answers provided during the 120-minute testing session.

The exam is a 120-minute, computer-based assessment. Candidates should plan to complete all 100 questions within this duration. It is recommended that you manage your time carefully across the six domains to ensure you have sufficient time to answer every question.

The exam price is $85 for civilians. For eligible military personnel, the exam is free via DANTES. Please verify your eligibility status and current pricing with your testing center or the official DSST website before scheduling your appointment.

editorial.overview: The Human Resource Management exam, certified by DSST, covers six key domains including HR planning, staffing, training, compensation, labor relations, and safety. This computer-based, 100-question exam assesses professional knowledge across these functional areas. It is currently active and available for test-takers seeking to demonstrate competency in managing human resources within an organizational framework. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in these business areas to earn college credit.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the six domains, which carry weights ranging from 9% to 12% of the total score. Focus on understanding the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, and the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Practice with multiple-choice questions to prepare for the 120-minute computer-based format. Check with DSST for the current certification path and additional study resources to ensure you are prepared for the testing environment.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is designed for students or professionals seeking college credit for human resource management knowledge. It is suitable for those with practical experience or academic training in personnel administration, labor relations, or general organizational management practices.
